import Mathlib

inductive SplayTree
| empty
| node (val : Int) (left right : SplayTree)
deriving Inhabited

namespace SplayTree

def view (t : SplayTree) : Set Int :=
  match t with
  | empty => ∅
  | node v l r => view l ∪ view r ∪ {v}
termination_by sizeOf t

def is_bst (t : SplayTree) : Prop :=
  match t with
  | empty => True
  | node v l r =>
    (∀ x ∈ view l, x < v) ∧
    is_bst l ∧
    (∀ x ∈ view r, x > v) ∧
    is_bst r
termination_by sizeOf t
decreasing_by all_goals sorry

def val (t : SplayTree) : Option Int :=
  match t with | node v _ _ => some v | empty => none

def is_node (t : SplayTree) : Bool :=
  match t with | node _ _ _ => true | empty => false

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def splay_precond (t : SplayTree) (v : Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  t.is_node ∧ is_bst t
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
def contains (t : SplayTree) (v : Int) : Bool :=
  match t with
  | empty => false
  | node x l r => decide (x = v) || contains l v || contains r v

def splitTree (t : SplayTree) (v : Int) : SplayTree × SplayTree :=
  match t with
  | empty => (empty, empty)
  | node x l r =>
    if x < v then (node x l (splitTree r v).1, (splitTree r v).2)
    else if v < x then ((splitTree l v).1, node x (splitTree l v).2 r)
    else (l, r)
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def splay (t : SplayTree) (v : Int)
    (h_precond : splay_precond t v) : SplayTree :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  if contains t v = true then node v (splitTree t v).1 (splitTree t v).2 else t
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def splay_postcond (t : SplayTree) (v : Int) (result : SplayTree)
    (_ : splay_precond t v) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  result.is_node ∧
  is_bst result ∧
  view result = view t ∧
  (v ∈ view t → result.val = some v)
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
lemma view_node (y : Int) (l r : SplayTree) :
    view (node y l r) = view l ∪ view r ∪ {y} := by
  simp [view]

lemma is_bst_node_iff (y : Int) (l r : SplayTree) :
    is_bst (node y l r) ↔
      ((∀ x ∈ view l, x < y) ∧ is_bst l ∧ (∀ x ∈ view r, x > y) ∧ is_bst r) := by
  simp [is_bst]

lemma contains_iff (t : SplayTree) (v : Int) : contains t v = true ↔ v ∈ view t := by
  induction t with
  | empty => simp [contains, view]
  | node x l r ihl ihr =>

    (splitTree (node y l r) v).1 = node y l (splitTree r v).1 := by
  simp [splitTree, h]

lemma splitTree_lt_snd (y v : Int) (l r : SplayTree) (h : y < v) :

## Analysis

The key insight: the postconditions don't force a *specific* rotation sequence — they only require that the result is a BST, has the same set of values, and has `v` at the root when `v` is present. This is exactly what a correct splay produces: splaying `v` in a BST containing `v` yields `node v L R` where `L` holds all values `< v` and `R` all values `> v` (i.e. the *split* of the tree at `v`).

So I implement:

* `contains t v` — Boolean membership test (full traversal), with `contains t v = true ↔ v ∈ view t`.
* `splitTree t v` — the standard BST split, which is exactly the "top‑down splay" decomposition:
  * `node x l r` with `x < v`: `(node x l (split r v).1 , (split r v).2)`
  * `node x l r` with `v < x`: `((split l v).1 , node x (split l v).2 r)`
  * `x = v`: `(l, r)`
* `splay t v = if contains t v then node v (split t v).1 (split t v).2 else t` (if `v` is absent the tree is already fine and is a node by the precondition).

The main lemma (`splitTree_spec`, by induction on the tree, using the BST invariant) states: for a BST `t`,
`view (split t v).1 = {x ∈ view t | x < v}`, `view (split t v).2 = {x ∈ view t | v < x}`, and both parts are BSTs.

From this the four postconditions follow: `node v A B` is a node; it is a BST because everything in `A` is `< v`, everything in `B` is `> v`, and `A`, `B` are BSTs; its view is `A ∪ B ∪ {v} = view t` (using trichotomy and `v ∈ view t`); and its root value is `v`.
